title: Al-Jazari, Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices
summary: Al-Jazari, chief engineer at the Artuqid court in Diyarbakir, finished writing his Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices in 1206 (602 AH), apparently shortly before his death. It has fifty chapters in six categories, covering clocks, drinking-session vessels and figures, washing vessels, fountains and water-raising machines, with 173 drawings.

uncertainty.note: One page gives 16 January 1206 for the author's completion; a surviving early copy was completed in 602 AH (April 1206 per the same page). A museum catalogue seen in a search gave 1198 to 1200 but could not be opened.

as_recorded.value: al-Jazari finished writing his book on 4 Jumada the Second, 602 H/ 16 January 1206
Al-Jazarī, who passed away in 1206, served as the chief engineer for the court of the Artuqids in Diyarbakir.

where.historical_name: Amid (Diyar Bakr), seat of the Artuqid ruler Nasir al-Din

importance.justification: A well-illustrated medieval treatise on automata, clocks and machines.
